newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA'S TAYLOR WINS TOSS AND BATS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA'S TAYLOR WINS TOSS AND BATS.

text.p: Australia captain Mark Taylor won the toss and elected to bat on the first day of the third test against West Indies at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Thursday.
Australia, who lead the five test series 2-0 and need only a draw to retain the Frank Worrell trophy, named all-rounder Michael Bevan as 12th man.
West Indies made one change from the side that lost the second test in Sydney, naming Junior Murray as wicketkeeper in place of Courtney Browne.
Batsman Adrian Griffith was selected as 12th man for the tourists, who dropped key batsman Brian Lara one place in the batting order to number four.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul was listed at number three in a direct swap with West Indies' vice-captain.
Despite their comfortable victories in the first two tests, Australia changed their batting line-up by recalling left-hander Justin Langer at the expense of number three Ricky Ponting.
Opener Matthew Hayden was also called up as a replacement for Matthew Elliott, who was ruled out because of a knee injury.
All-rounder Steve Waugh, who missed the second test because of a groin strain, returned to strengthen Australia's middle order.
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Hayden, Justin Langer, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Greg Blewett, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath, Michael Bevan 12th man,

West Indies - Sherwin Campbell, Robert Samuels, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Junior Murray, Ian Bishop, Curtly Ambrose, Kenny Benjamin, Courtney Walsh (captain), Adrian Griffith 12th man.
